clue.text: Oral surgeon's first name revealed in Punch? Just the opposite

indicators.note: revealed in says one piece shows up inside another, here the name inside the punch
Just the opposite flips the containment just described, so the punch goes inside instead
first says only the opening letter of the word surgeon's is used

parts.note: to punch is to poke, jab

explanation.surface: A question about whether a dental surgeon's first name was given away in the puppet show or comic Punch.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, N goes inside POKE; 'Just the opposite' reverses that, so POKE sits between S and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoken and oral both describe something said aloud rather than written, as in an oral or spoken agreement.

clue.text: Save or discard?

definitions.meaning: to put by or reserve, such as money for later
to dismiss or reject, such as a court overturning a verdict

explanation.surface: A question of whether to keep something or throw it out.
explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase means both keep for later and annul, as in a judge overturning a ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase can mean reserve for future use or quash and annul, covering both opposed senses.

clue.text: Concerned with anything that is seen as supervision

parts.note: over can mean concerning, as in a row over money
a sight is anything that is seen

explanation.surface: A definition of watching over people as being about whatever is visible.
explanation.definitionFit: Oversight means watchful management or control, the same as supervision.

clue.text: Always part without a hint of sadness

indicators.note: without says a letter is removed from the word for part

parts.note: to part is to sever, cut off

indicators.note: a hint of picks just the opening letter of sadness

explanation.surface: A wish to always separate without any sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever means at all times, as in 'ever hopeful', a synonym of always.

clue.text: Whip animal to gain speed? Not at first

parts.note: a lamb is a young animal

indicators.note: Not at first says the opening letter of the word for speed is dropped

parts.note: haste means speed

explanation.surface: Advice to flog an animal so it goes faster, then a hesitation about doing so at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambaste is to criticise harshly or thrash, so it shares the figurative sense of whip, to lash out at.

clue.text: Mean to prevent missing the last time

indicators.note: missing the last says the final letter of the word for prevent goes

parts.note: to avert is to prevent
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: An intention to stop someone missing the last train or bus.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic the mean is the average, the sum divided by the number of values.

clue.text: Reportedly forbidden to use lorries right away as ammunition carriers

indicators.note: Reportedly says the word for forbidden is taken as it sounds when said

parts.note: banned means forbidden

indicators.note: use says the remaining letters are put to work in a new order
away says the letter for right is taken out of lorries

explanation.surface: A ban on using lorries to move ammunition, said to be in force at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'at once' but removes R from LORRIES, leaving LORIES, which 'use' rearranges into OLIERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandoliers are belts worn over the shoulder with pockets or loops that hold cartridges.

clue.text: Letters from Amundsen seditious in opinion

indicators.note: Letters from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Roald Amundsen, the polar explorer, writing rebellious letters expressing his views.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition took in 'in', a link word: the answer means opinion, and 'in opinion' would not stand in for it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sense can mean a general feeling or view, as in the sense of a meeting.

clue.text: Without getting minister to reach out

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
to minister to someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: Trying to make contact without the help of a government minister.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend is to stretch out, such as a hand reaching forward.

clue.text: Knight leaving to switch allegiance in secret

indicators.note: leaving says the knight's letter departs from the word for switching allegiance

parts.note: to convert is to change one's faith or side
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight quietly deserting to change sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Covert means concealed or done in secret, as in covert operations.

clue.text: Thus deleting conclusion of article before getting a word of warning

indicators.note: deleting conclusion of says the final letter of the article is removed

parts.note: the is the definite article
ere is an old word for before
fore is what golfers shout as a warning

explanation.surface: Instructions for editing a document: cut the end of an article, then add a warning.
explanation.walkthrough: FORE is the golfer's shout to warn people a ball is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are formal connectives meaning consequently, introducing a conclusion drawn from what came before.

clue.text: Not one tenor in this group of performers

parts.note: none means not one
T is the abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: A complaint that a vocal ensemble lacks a single tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a set of nine musicians or singers, so a specific kind of performing group.

clue.text: Indifferent when sailor's grabbed by drunk? Not entirely

indicators.note: grabbed by says the sailor is held inside the shortened drunk
Not entirely says the last letter of the drunk is cut off

parts.note: a sot is a drunk
OS, ordinary seaman, is a sailor; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A sailor seized by a drunkard, asking whether that counts as mediocre.
explanation.definitionFit: So-so means mediocre or middling, the sense of indifferent in 'an indifferent performance'.

clue.text: Hurry up with denial over backing pal employed by Gove earlier

indicators.note: earlier says the Gove part comes first, before the reversed denial
employed by says the reversed pal is put to work inside the politician's name

parts.note: Michael Gove is a British Conservative politician

indicators.note: backing says the word for pal is read backwards

parts.note: a mate is a pal

indicators.note: over says the denial is turned over, read backwards

parts.note: no is a denial

explanation.surface: A political scene: someone urging haste while denying things and backing a friend whom Michael Gove once employed.
explanation.walkthrough: Michael Gove is a British Conservative politician. 'backing' reverses the pal and 'over' turns the denial round; 'earlier' puts the Gove part first.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal idiom urging someone to be quick, exactly what hurry up says.

clue.text: Wildly extravagant design of fragile pot

indicators.note: design of says the letters are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A delicate pot whose design is over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: Profligate means recklessly wasteful with money or resources.

clue.text: Jog right around in turn stopping to take rest at the end

indicators.note: stopping says the turn with right inside plugs the gap in the other piece, like a stopper

parts.note: to do someone is to take or cheat them

indicators.note: at the end says only the final letter of rest is used
in says the reversed right goes inside the turn

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in 'your go'

indicators.note: around says the abbreviation for right is read backwards

explanation.surface: Running instructions: turn right, stop, and finally take a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' reverses the right, 'in' puts it inside the turn, and that unit is 'stopping' the gap between 'to take' and the last letter of rest; 'to take' means to cheat.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogtrot is a gentle easy trot, a steady jogging pace.

clue.text: Reveal fellow needing no introduction at church

indicators.note: needing no introduction says the man's name loses its opening letter

parts.note: Kevin is a man's name, so a fellow
CE is Church of England

explanation.surface: A man so well known at church that he needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing no introduction' sounds like praise of fame but strips the first letter from KEVIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince is to show or make evident a feeling or quality, a formal synonym of reveal.

clue.text: In agreement with social worker about working with boy at first

indicators.note: at first says these pieces come before the social worker

parts.note: C, for circa, means about
on means working, as with a machine switched on
a son is a boy
an ant is a social insect, and a worker ant

explanation.surface: A social worker on a case concerning a boy, apparently in agreement with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'social worker' is not a caseworker but an ant, a social insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Consonant with means in harmony or agreeing with, as in findings consonant with theory.

clue.text: Morally corrupt rebel feeding a negative effect

indicators.note: feeding says the rebel goes into the negative effect

parts.note: a dent is a setback, a negative effect, as in a dent in profits
Jack Cade led a rebellion in England in 1450

explanation.surface: A rebel's corrupt influence feeding a harmful outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led a revolt in Kent in 1450, so he is the crossword rebel.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent describes moral decline and self-indulgence, a synonym of corrupt.

clue.text: Prevent small fairy taking it back

indicators.note: back says the fairy and the word it are read in reverse order

parts.note: an elf is a kind of fairy

explanation.surface: Stopping a tiny fairy from taking something back.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle is to suppress or hold in, which stops something from happening.

clue.text: Abridgement of largely impressive book

indicators.note: largely says most, but not all, of the word for impressive is used

parts.note: epic means impressive, grand in scale
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A shortened version of a mostly impressive book.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome can be a summary or condensed account of a longer work.

clue.text: Unusual compass found on street

indicators.note: found on says the compass sits after the street in this across entry

parts.note: compass means range or scope

explanation.surface: Someone picks up an odd compass lying in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Strange and unusual are plain synonyms for something out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Humiliate in game

definitions.meaning: to crush or put someone down
a racket sport played in a walled court

explanation.surface: Thrashing someone in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to crush someone and is also the racket sport played against walls.

clue.text: Split up mischievous sons before start of recital

indicators.note: before says these letters come ahead of the recital letter
up says, in a down entry, the following words are read upward, in reverse

parts.note: evil means wicked or mischievous

indicators.note: start of picks the opening letter of recital

explanation.surface: Splitting up naughty boys before a performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split up' reads as one phrase, but 'up' reverses EVIL and S in this down clue; 'Split' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To sliver is to split or cut something into thin pieces.

clue.text: Girl in retrospect almost lay with old American wanton

indicators.note: in retrospect says the girl's name is read looking back, in reverse

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name

indicators.note: almost says the word for lay loses its last letter

parts.note: lay means not clerical, so civil

explanation.surface: Looking back, a girl nearly slept with an old American lothario.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanton in its older sense means sexually unrestrained, the meaning of lascivious.

clue.text: Large raise to join top firm

indicators.note: raise says, in a down entry, the letters for large are lifted, read upward

parts.note: OS, outsize, means large
a lid is a top

explanation.surface: A large pay rise for joining a top company.
explanation.definitionFit: Solid and firm both describe something hard and stable.

clue.text: Star turn close to Virginia

indicators.note: turn says the word for close to is turned round

parts.note: on can mean close to, as in a town on the coast
VA is the abbreviation for the US state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A celebrity's performance near Virginia, a star turn being a headline act.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that suddenly flares to great brightness and then fades.

clue.text: A rich source of Vitamin B? Not half

indicators.note: Not half says the first half of the vitamin's name is dropped

parts.note: thiamine is vitamin B1

explanation.surface: A question about a food rich in vitamin B, answered with the slang 'not half', meaning very much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' looks like British slang for 'absolutely', but it removes half of THIAMINE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mine is a rich source, as in a mine of information.

clue.text: Taken from weevil larvae discovered in house

indicators.note: Taken from says the letters are lifted out of the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Grubs removed after being found infesting a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country or suburban house.

clue.text: Persistent noise bat produces over time

indicators.note: produces says these letters are worked up into something new

explanation.surface: A bat keeps up a noise over a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate means stubbornly persisting, refusing to give way.

clue.text: Soldiers considered being paid off

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
deemed means considered or judged

explanation.surface: Troops judged to have been bribed.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt or mortgage that has been cleared is described as redeemed, settled in full.

clue.text: Scarper when up to something criminal on the borders of Belize

indicators.note: on says the criminal piece sits after the borders in this across entry
the borders of picks the outside letters of the country's name

parts.note: at it means up to mischief or wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A crook fleeing over the frontier of Belize while up to no good.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarper is British slang for run away.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is a slangy order to leave fast, just as scarper means to flee.
